style_authority.note: The design read restates the restrained, dense-but-calm enterprise character. M6 maps treatments to "existing token roles" with "No marketing hero treatment", and it notes that "Dense data itself is appropriate for this audience."

reference_selection.note: Uses the relevant design-craft moves ("Flat KPI grid -> priority hierarchy", "Dashboard card soup -> decision surface", "Decorative chart -> diagnostic evidence") and the L0/L1 evidence tiers. It applies less visible dashboard framing than the others: no surface mode or treatment variant, and no calibration cap.

anti_generic_redesign.note: Frames the problem as a decision sequence ("scope and freshness -> priority exception -> supporting evidence -> next action") and promotes the work object over the overview cards. The repair doesn't depend on card chrome.

evidence_level.note: States "L0 static - prose description only" and gives a provisional 60-74 band, calling it "a directional assessment". It lists typography, polish, accessibility and implementation as "unscored".

verified_boundary.note: Separates Established / Inferred / Unverified. Each finding also has a "Runtime unknown" column, and it says "Unmentioned features are not assumed absent" and that no browser validation was performed.

design_moves.note: Covers a lead operational state plus a supporting metric strip (M1), an exception queue as a prioritized view of the table (M2), a task-first table (M3) and a context band (M6). The moves are folded into the findings table, so the queue structure is less fully specified than it could be.

scope_control.note: Very tight: 44 lines, 4 blockers and exactly 8 moves. Everything stays within dashboard UI quality and pre-implementation validation.
